## Objectives

- Understand how to use Git, GitHub and Markdown.
- Create and manage repositories on GitHub.
- Write and format documentation using Markdown.
- Share and collaborate effectively using Git and GitHub, with SSH
  authentication and **signed commits**.

# Git

## Git

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
- A version control system (VCS).
- Created in 2005 by Linus Torvalds.
- Efficiently tracks changes in files.
- Manages source code and documentation within a project.
:::
::: {.column width="40%"}
![](https://git-scm.com/images/logos/downloads/Git-Logo-2Color.svg){width="80%"}
:::
:::

## Architecture

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
- Remote repository (server, `origin`) and local **clones**.
- Fully **distributed**: each clone contains the full history; work
  offline.
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
![](https://wac-cdn.atlassian.com/dam/jcr:9d51f0ee-5946-4be2-886c-ff040ef8c1a1/03.svg)
:::
:::

## Commits, hashes and tags

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
- Commits = snapshots of the repository.
- Each commit has a unique, unalterable **hash**.
- **Tags** name commits, often releases.
- **Signed commits** prove authorship → "Verified" badge.
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
![](https://wac-cdn.atlassian.com/dam/jcr:bb02240a-7d85-4f5a-ae7f-c2727b37fc79/01%20Many%20ways%20of%20referring%20to%20a%20commit.svg)
:::
:::

## The three areas

1. **Working directory**: the files you edit.
2. **Staging area**: what goes into the next commit (`git add`).
3. **Repository**: the committed history (`git commit`).

`git status` tells you where every change currently is.

## Branches

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
- A branch = a movable pointer to a commit.
- Default branch: `main`.
- Work on features and fixes without touching `main`.
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
![](https://wac-cdn.atlassian.com/dam/jcr:34c86360-8dea-4be4-92f7-6597d4d5bfae/02%20Feature%20branches.svg)
:::
:::

## Merging branches

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
- **Merge**: the default; what we use in this course.
- **Rebase**: replay commits, linear history.
- **Squash**: collapse a branch into one commit.
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
![](https://wac-cdn.atlassian.com/dam/jcr:4639eeb8-e417-434a-a3f8-a972277fc66a/02%20Merging%20main%20into%20the%20feature%20branh.svg)
:::
:::

## Conflicts

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
- Arise when the **same lines** are edited on both sides.
- Git detects them and asks **you** to resolve.
- Tricky at first, and a crucial skill. You will practice it today,
  on purpose.
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
![](https://imgs.xkcd.com/comics/git.png){height="450"}
:::
:::

## Ignore files

- `.gitignore` lists what Git must **not** track.
- Cleanliness (no build artifacts) and security (no secrets).
- Commit **source files only**: never `target/`, never binaries.
- Tip: avoid gitignore generators; too many unnecessary rules.

## Summary: Git

- Git is a distributed VCS.
- Commits track changes; branches track parallel versions.
- Merge, rebase or squash bring work back together.
- Conflicts are detected, and resolved by you.

**Learn Git from the command line: it works everywhere, even on a
server.**

# GitHub

## GitHub

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
- Git hosting platform, created in 2008.
- The home of most open source projects.
- Where your practical works will live.
:::
::: {.column width="40%"}
![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/91/Octicons-mark-github.svg){width="60%"}
:::
:::

## Social platform

- Follow users, star projects, discover code.
- Your profile is a **portfolio**; recruiters look at it.
- **Fork** repositories: copy, change, contribute back.
- Free **Pro** account for students; apply with your HEIG-VD email
  (GitHub Education).

## Users and organizations

- Repositories belong to a **user** or an **organization**.
- Organizations share repositories between members.
- This course lives in one: **github.com/heigvd-dai-26**; each PW
  team can create its own.

## Issues, pull requests and forks

1. Open an **issue** to discuss the change (optional, recommended).
2. Clone (or fork) and checkout a new **branch**.
3. Commit and push as often as you want.
4. Create the **pull request**.
5. A teammate reviews and merges if OK.
6. Delete the branch.

The workflow of your practical works, and of the industry.

## The rejected push

```text
! [rejected]  main -> main (fetch first)
```

- Not broken: a teammate pushed to `main` before you.
- Fix: `git pull` (rebase), resolve if needed, `git push`.
- Practice it **before** it happens under deadline pressure.

# Markdown

## Markdown

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
- Lightweight markup language.
- Created by John Gruber and Aaron Swartz in 2004.
- Simple, versatile, everywhere: READMEs, issues, wikis, sites.
:::
::: {.column width="40%"}
![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/48/Markdown-mark.svg){width="60%"}
:::
:::

## Markdown and output formats

- Plain text in, many formats out: web pages, PDF, slides.
- **Diffable**: Git shows which *sentence* changed; a `.docx` cannot.
- This deck and the whole course site are written in a flavour of
  Markdown ([Quarto](https://quarto.org/)'s `.qmd`).

## Syntax

```markdown
# Heading      **bold**  _italic_  `code`

- bullet          1. numbered      > quote

[link](https://heig-vd.ch)   ![alt](diagram.png)

| Column | Column |
| ------ | -----: |
```

- Fenced code blocks: three backticks **+ the language**.
- Same conventions as Discord, Telegram, etc.

## Specifications

- No single standard.
- **CommonMark**: the strict specification.
- **GitHub Flavored Markdown**: CommonMark + tables, task lists,
  strikethrough. What you write on GitHub.

## Summary: Markdown

- Easy to learn and use.
- Documentation, READMEs, reports, and slides.
- Exports to many formats.
